clearedSpotChecks.check: 2,000 of the model vectors sent by eth_call to the tools/opdiff battery dispatcher placed by state override, twice per chain (42161, 4663), bracketed by web3_clientVersion.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Checked independently with my own vectors and my own bytecode. web3_clientVersion on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc and https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com both returned nitro/v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f-20261116T155937Z/linux-arm64/go1.27.3 on 2026-11-27. I placed an 18 byte program (CALLDATALOAD three words, one opcode, MSTORE, RETURN) by state override and sent 390 eth_calls per chain covering MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, EXP, SLT and SGT, with 70 percent of operands drawn from edges (0, 1, 2^255, 2^256-1, 2^128, 2^96, 2^64, int24 minimum and maximum, MIN_TICK and MAX_TICK, shift amounts 255 to 257) and seed 2711. Every result equalled the Python integer result: 0 mismatches and 0 errors on both chains. The test covers what the public RPC nodes execute; it cannot show which build the sequencer runs, which the review cannot observe.

clearedSpotChecks.check: codeBitmapInternal and validJumpdest of both binaries in the models: the PoolManager accepts exactly the 610 JUMPDEST bytes outside push data and rejects the 29 inside push data; all 418 distinct push-constant targets of JUMP and JUMPI are valid.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched the deployed PoolManager runtime with eth_getCode at 0x360e68faccca8ca495c1b759fd9eee466db9fb32 (42161) and 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951 (4663) and walked it in Python. Both are 24,009 bytes, with 610 JUMPDEST bytes outside push data, 29 0x5b bytes inside push data and 418 distinct PUSH-then-JUMP/JUMPI constants, all of which land on a valid JUMPDEST. The counts in the cleared item match the deployed code exactly. The code is not reached by any JUMP whose target an ordinary caller supplies, since all targets are push constants or return addresses the compiler pushed.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Which src/ lines depend on these routines: FullMath.mulDiv MULMOD(a, b, not(0)), MULMOD(a, b, denominator) and DIV; TickBitmap.compress SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD, SLT; flipTick SDIV and SAR.
clearedSpotChecks.note: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 reads mulmod(a, b, not(0)), :35 div(prod0, denominator), :48 mulmod(a, b, denominator), and :30 require(denominator > prod1) guards zero and overflow. src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:19-26 compress uses signextend(2, .), sdiv, smod and slt; :64 sdiv and :67 sar(8, tick) feed the keccak slot at :69. My eth_call vectors on both chains included the exact operand shapes these lines use (signextend byte index 2 on int24 edges, sar by 8, mulmod by 2^256-1) and all matched. The item clears Nitro arithmetic only; it says nothing about storage, transient storage or call-family behaviour, which the unit correctly left as leads.
